title: Greek roots II
lede: The Greek roots behind the words for people, power, feeling and form, plus how scientists still build new words from them.

sections.md:
## Where Greek words live
Latin gave English most of its everyday and legal vocabulary. **Greek** gave it the vocabulary of **ideas, science, medicine and government**. When someone coins a new technical word today, like *cryptocurrency*, they still reach for Greek. Learn these roots and you can read the vocabulary of every field you'll ever study.

## People and power
| Root | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **anthrop** | human | anthropology, philanthropy, misanthrope |
| **dem** | the people | democracy, epidemic, demographic |
| **crat, cracy** | rule, power | bureaucracy, autocrat, aristocracy, technocrat |
| **arch** | rule, chief; also ancient | monarchy, anarchy, archbishop; archaeology, archive |
| **phil** | love | philosophy, philanthropy, bibliophile |
| **phob** | fear | phobia, claustrophobia, xenophobia |

## Mind, feeling and belief
| Root | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **path** | feeling; disease | empathy, sympathy, apathy; pathology, psychopath |
| **dox** | opinion, belief | orthodox, paradox, heterodox |
| **ortho** | straight, correct | orthodox, orthodontist, orthopedic |
| **gno, gnos** | know | diagnosis, prognosis, agnostic |

## Form, kind and number
| Root | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **morph** | shape, form | metamorphosis, amorphous, morphology |
| **gen** | birth, origin, kind | genesis, genetics, generate, homogeneous |
| **homo / hetero** | same / different | homogeneous, homonym / heterogeneous |
| **onym, nym** | name, word | synonym, antonym, pseudonym, anonymous, acronym |
| **pseudo** | false | pseudonym, pseudoscience |
| **poly / mono** | many / one | polygon, polymath / monopoly, monotone |
| **pan** | all | pandemic, panorama, panacea |

## Hidden, power and motion
| Root | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **crypt** | hidden, secret | cryptic, encrypt, cryptocurrency, crypt |
| **dyna** | power | dynamic, dynamite, dynasty |
| **kine, cine** | movement | kinetic, cinema, telekinesis |

## The Greek negative: a- and an-
Greek uses **a-** (before consonants) or **an-** (before vowels) to mean *without*. You already know *atom* (a- + tom, cut: uncuttable). Now read these:

| Word | Parts | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| apathy | a- + path | without feeling: not caring |
| anarchy | an- + arch | without a ruler |
| anonymous | an- + onym | without a name |
| amorphous | a- + morph | without a definite shape |
| agnostic | a- + gnos | without knowledge (of whether God exists) |

sections.q: Someone who is **apathetic** about the election…
sections.why: **a-** (without) + **path** (feeling). No feeling about it either way.

sections.md:
## -cracy vs -archy
Both mean *rule*, but they ask different questions. **-cracy** asks *who has the power*: democracy (the people), autocracy (one self), bureaucracy (the desk, from French *bureau*: officials), technocracy (technical experts). **-archy** asks *how many are in charge*: monarchy (one), oligarchy (a few), anarchy (none).

sections.title: Decode a compound
steps: Love of humanity, shown through giving.

sections.title: Decode a puzzle word
steps: **para-** = beside, beyond, contrary to. **dox** = opinion, belief.
Something beyond what you'd expect: a statement that seems to contradict itself but may still be true.
sections.answer: "The more you sweat in training, the less you bleed in a fight" is a **paradox**: more pain now means less pain later.

sections.title: Decode a modern coinage
steps: **crypt** = hidden, secret. Cryptography is the science of secret writing.
**currency** = money (Latin *currere*, to run: money runs from hand to hand).
sections.answer: **Money secured by cryptography**: hidden codes, not a central bank.

sections.md:
## Why scientists still use Greek
Greek builds long, precise words by stacking roots, often joined with an **-o-**: psych**o**logy, therm**o**meter, hydr**o**phobia. Doctors use it to name things exactly: *gastr* (stomach) + *-itis* (inflammation) = **gastritis**. *Cardi* (heart) + *-o-* + *logy* = **cardiology**. Once you know the parts, a 6-syllable medical word is just a sentence written short.

sections.label: Common traps
sections.md:
- **Homo- (Greek, same) vs homo (Latin, human).** *Homogeneous* is Greek *homos*: of the same kind. *Homo sapiens* is Latin *homo*: human being. Same spelling, different languages.
- **Empathy vs sympathy.** **Sym-** (with) + path = feeling *for* someone: you feel sorry. **Em-** (in) + path = feeling *into* someone: you feel what they feel.
- **Gen** is in both Greek and Latin (*genus*, kind). Same idea either way: birth, origin, kind.

practice.q: Type the word: **pseudo** (false) + **onym** (name) = a fake name an author writes under.
practice.why: **pseudonym**. Mark Twain was Samuel Clemens's pseudonym.
**pan** (all) + *akos* (remedy). A cure-all. Usually used skeptically: "There's no panacea for a bad economy."

practice.q: Which word means rule by **one** person?

practice.hint: You know **anthrop**. The front means the opposite of *phil*.

practice.why: *klepto* (steal, as in kleptomaniac) + **cracy** (rule): rule by thieves.

practice.q: A doctor gives a **prognosis**. She is telling you…
options: how it will likely turn out
practice.why: **pro-** (before) + **gnos** (know): knowing beforehand. A *diagnosis* (*dia-*, through) identifies the disease; a *prognosis* predicts its course.

practice.q: A person who has mastered **many** fields of learning is a **poly**___ . Type the full word.
practice.why: **polymath**: **poly** (many) + *math* (learning; Greek *mathema*, lesson). Leonardo da Vinci is the classic example.
practice.hint: The second part is the Greek word that also gave us *mathematics*.
